body:
Both dropped. `reduce_both_engines` is now `evaluator_and_stepper_agree`, which is just the property's own name — and `eval_after_literal_edit` became `incremental_agrees_with_fresh_after_edit`.

On the return type: both helpers now produce a `verdict` (`Holds` / `Fails(rendered)` / `Vacuous`) defined at the top of the file, and the `Equality.semantic.exp` comparison moved inside them — previously each caller redid it, which was the actual duplication. Two readers of a verdict:

- `holds` — QCheck predicate; prints the rendered disagreement and returns false only on `Fails`.
- `check_still_fails(~issue, ~property, verdict)` — the counterexample; passes on `Fails`, and on `Holds` fails with `<issue url> looks fixed: re-enable the `\`'`X`' property, delete this`.

`Vacuous` is its own case rather than folded into either, so a filtered case can't be read as evidence in either direction — and a counterexample that stops reaching a result gets told to re-minimize instead of silently passing.

body:
Right — Alcotest already has it: `neg : 'a testable -> 'a testable`, a testable with negated equality. The `verdict` type, `holds` and `check_still_fails` are all gone.

There's now one parameterized check per property, taking the `testable` and `msg` that `Alcotest.check` takes anyway:

```reason
let check_evaluator_against_stepper =
    (~step_limit: int, ~testable: testable(Exp.t), ~msg: string, uexp: Exp.t): bool
```

The property passes `testable_core_exp`; the counterexample passes `neg(testable_core_exp)` plus a message naming the property to re-enable. Same function, same comparison, opposite expectation. `testable_core_exp` came back because Alcotest renders both expressions itself on failure, which is better than the string I was building by hand.

The `bool` is "did it actually compare anything" — the properties discard it, and the counterexamples assert it, so one that stops reaching a result gets told to re-minimize rather than silently passing. Verified both directions: pointing the pin at `fun (x::y) -> x` (no duplicate binder, so the two agree) fails with `#2128 looks fixed: re-enable ...`, and forcing the case vacuous fails with `counterexample still reduces under both; re-minimize it otherwise`.
